final_decision.order: blur_glass -> compression_jpeg (physical order: optical blur before storage; 8x8 JPEG grid remains intact/sharp in flat regions => JPEG is last, not blurred afterwards)
final_decision.tier_note: two steps, no noise category (glass shuffle is stochastic but belongs to blur)
final_decision.rationale: JPEG presence is certain (0%-FP block_boundary signal). The blur DT selects glass (glass_score>0.25, sigma<3, anisotropy<1.7); gaussian/lens/motion are excluded by 2.0-2.2 dB worse PSNR (motion) and by visual texture (gaussian/lens too smooth/vivid). Absolute PSNR stays ~25.5-26.3 dB for every candidate because the glass shuffle realization cannot be pixel-matched; the skill explicitly forbids chasing PSNR for non-deterministic (glass) blur. No noise (raw sigma 0.74; peeled 1.48 lower bound; structured residual) and no global step (all legal global functions overshoot: contrast_weaken_scale:1 -> std ratio 0.75 vs target 0.90; saturate_weaken:1 -> chroma 0.6-0.7 vs target 0.886; brightness shift/gamma sev1 -> mean shift >=20 vs +5; quantization ruled out by unique_G=211).
final_decision.unexplained_residual: Target photometrics vs glass3+jpeg4 simulation: channel std ratio ~0.90 (target std 55.25 vs sim 61.29) and channel means +4.7/+3.2/+8.3 (overall +5.1). Best affine description ~0.90*x + 12.6, i.e. a mild gamma-like tone curve that no legal x_distortion global severity matches (minimum-severity functions all overshoot). Residual is structured (spatial_corr 0.97), contributing to the ~25.5 dB PSNR ceiling together with the stochastic glass shuffle.

support_pairs_analysis.setup: degraded.png/clean.png of the target are byte-identical (md5) to support pair 0. Supports 1-4 are different clean images; each was analyzed with run_full_analysis.py (reports in /tmp/E6A_0017_rep3_support1..4.json).
support_pairs_analysis.cross_image_consistency: All five pairs: JPEG present with very strong blockiness (bb 4.2-7.3, 0%FP signal), strong blur (gm 0.18-0.51), no reliable noise (sigma estimates 0.37-2.47 scatter with content and are artifact-driven; §B on the target's peeled residual shows no noise), and inconsistent global verdicts across pairs (saturation/contrast flags flip between pairs while mean shift stays small; variance ratios 0.65-0.79 scatter as expected for content-dependent blur, not for a fixed global contrast scale). This supports the core pipeline JPEG+strong blur with no noise/global; glass_score is 1.22-1.52 on every pair, so it is not by itself discriminative between blur subtypes, but the target's own DT path (anisotropy 1.445<1.7) selects glass.
support_pairs_analysis.support2_cross_check: Same-candidate test on pair2 (different content, sigma=1.48): glass3+jpeg4 = 25.70 dB CI 7/10; gaussian4+jpeg4 = 27.84 dB CI 8/10. Same pattern as the target (PSNR prefers gaussian by ~2 dB; 1:1 crops show the blurred target keeps the mottled pixel-shuffle texture of glass, while gaussian/lens are smoother and more vivid). Consistent with glass being the true stochastic blur.
